mechanism: Amphotericin B causes acute nephrotoxicity that significantly increases cyclosporine levels by reducing renal clearance, while cyclosporine itself impairs renal function, creating a synergistic nephrotoxic effect.
action: Monitor serum creatinine and cyclosporine levels closely; consider alternative antifungal agents (fluconazole, itraconazole) when possible; use lipid formulations of amphotericin B if combination is necessary; ensure adequate hydration and monitor for acute kidney injury.
